cells.tense: The pen is in your hand and the thinking is landing here, right now.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin a small piece of something — a question, a sketch, a first draft — with no end decided, and see where it wants to head.
cells.core:
You can find the clean line fast. When something is tangled — a decision, a conflict, a set of numbers that will not add up — you cut through the noise, say what holds, and the table gets a fairer picture because you were sitting at it.
What keeps this from going cold is the willingness to start before anything is settled. Fairness on a table like this is not only deciding what is owed. It is leaving room for what has not been said yet, and the piece of you that begins things without knowing where they go is the one that keeps the room alive. Begin something with no end in sight and ask openly where it is heading. A fairness that only judges gets brittle; a fairness that begins can keep going.
cells.sheetLine: You cut to what holds, and the table gets fairer for it.
cells.verb: cutting through to the clean line while others are still talking
cells.place: a table where what is owed is being settled

cells.tense: You are already living past this moment, bracing at a fair call nobody has asked you for.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Take the call you have been rehearsing and make it — once, plainly, where people can see it, with no dry run past anybody.
cells.core:
On a table like this, the scales get weighed before anything has been set on them. You can see three moves ahead, so the call keeps being made inside your head, for the whole room, without the room. The clean line is still there. What has gone missing is the table it was meant to serve.
The weight here is unreal because none of it has happened yet. What carries it back is a move made once, where people can watch it happen: name the line, go first, and answer to something real rather than to your forecast. Starting the move yourself is what gives others room to move at all. Say the call and see where it lands.

cells.tense: You are still standing at the door of a decision that is already behind you.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Show one person here what fairness looks like by doing it beside them — one shared task, your hands in it too, no explanation owed after.
cells.core:
The clean line was here once and you could see it. Now the talk stays general, and what is fair gets handed to whoever is loudest or last to speak. You can feel what is off. You are not saying it in this room.
The way back runs through another person, not a principle. Do the fair thing next to someone instead of describing it — share the task, show it with your hands, and skip the lecture afterward. Meaning travels when it is carried, not when it is explained. One shared piece of work puts something real on the table, and the fair call has something to lean on. Do it once, together, and call that enough.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the fair call. You are not saying it aloud.

cells.tense: The pen is down while the room still moves through your hand.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: When someone brings you something that stings of unfair, sit with it a minute unsorted — no correcting, no rebalancing, no verdict at the close.
cells.core:
Half the fairness at this table was worked out by you, and telling it back, you would say the table mostly settles itself. The even calls, the lines that hold, the thing that keeps the room workable — your hand has been on the pen, and you have been calling that the table's own way.
Before you were the one cutting through, you were the one who could sit with somebody's mess and not flinch. Go back there. Hold one person's feeling without correcting it, without evening it out, without a fair call at the close. Do not fuse with it — stay near it. The balance you believe was happening without you turns out to be your attention, and attention is easier to give when you are not also saying it is not yours.
